Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 1 · Mon Aug 31 – Fri Sept 4, 2026 Grades 1–3

September: Soccer, Terry Fox and football

1 Say My Name Rock, Paper, Scissors

Locomotor & listen · Grades 1–6 · New Games

A quick way to learn everyone’s name in the first week.

Equipment: None (music optional)

Set-up: Open floor space or a cleared classroom. Music optional.

How we play:
  1. Students move around the space using the locomotor skill the teacher calls (walk, skip, gallop, side-step).
  2. On the signal, each student finds a partner and plays Rock, Paper, Scissors.
  3. The winner says their own name and their partner's name out loud (“I'm Sam, and you're Lee!”).
  4. Both partners high-five or elbow-bump, then move off to find a new partner.
  5. Play 6–10 rounds.

Cues: Find someone you have not played yet. · Say names clearly and kindly. · Freeze on the whistle — face the teacher.

Safety: Walk or skip with eyes up; no running into the centre of the room to find partners. Keep hands in your own space when you play. Stop signal: one whistle, freeze and face the teacher.

2 Here, There, Everywhere

Locomotor & listen · Big-Group Games

Teaches the stop and travel signals you will use all year.

Equipment: None

Set-up: Teacher is the pointer. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Spread out so you cannot touch a neighbour with an arm stretched. First command is a walk.
  2. Here = move toward the teacher. There = move where they point. Everywhere = scatter.
  3. Change locomotor each round.
  4. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.
  5. If you miss a signal, skip the next one and rejoin — no extra laps as punishment.

Cues: Here = toward the teacher. There = away. Everywhere = scatter. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Move the way I named (walk, skip, gallop) — not a race. · Stop in a balanced shape: two feet, knees soft.

Safety: Give a hoop of space. Freeze means still feet — not a last-second shove.

3 Kangaroos and Crocodiles

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Listen for your team name, then race home: a first-week listening game.

Equipment: None · two home lines and a centre line

Set-up: Teams on a centre line, facing you. Homes behind each.

How we play:
  1. Call ‘Kangaroos’ or ‘Crocodiles.’
  2. The named team turns and runs (or hops) home. The other team tags.
  3. Tagged players do 5 jumps and re-enter.

Cues: Wait for the name. · Tagged players jump 5 and re-enter next call. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft two-finger or noodle tags on the back or shoulder — never the head.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 1 · Mon Aug 31 – Fri Sept 4, 2026 Grades 4–6

September: Soccer, Terry Fox and football

1 Everybody’s It

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Everyone can tag, so the whole class is moving from the first minute.

Equipment: Optional one soft ball or spot markers · optional clothespins

Set-up: Court marked. Soft two-finger tags. Show the cost.

How we play:
  1. On go, tag anyone.
  2. If two people tag at once, RPS. The slower pose does 3 squats. Both stay in.
  3. Keep playing until the whistle.

Cues: Everyone tags. · RPS, then both stay in. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft two-finger or noodle tags on the back or shoulder — never the head.

2 Foosball Soccer

Invasion & team · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Short passes along a row teach first touch and passing lanes.

Equipment: Pool noodles; soccer balls; two goals

Set-up: Players in rows across the gym holding noodles to link with teammates (like foosball rods).

How we play:
  1. Rows can move sideways only, staying linked.
  2. Kick the ball toward the other team’s goal.
  3. Break the line (drop the noodle link) = turnover to the other team.
  4. Rotate rows so everyone plays forward and back.

Cues: Rows can move sideways only, staying linked. · Kick the ball toward the other team’s goal. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: Soft balls, spread out, no slide tackles. Heads up when the ball is loose.

3 3-Ball Soccer

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Three balls at once mean more touches and quick decisions.

Equipment: 3 soccer balls

Set-up: Play soccer with THREE balls at once. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Use regular soccer rules otherwise (feet, out of bounds, goalies optional).
  2. Any ball that enters the goal counts. Restart that ball at centre or from the goalie.
  3. Heads up — three balls means more traffic. Foam balls in a gym. Ideal for large classes.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball. · Find a passing lane, not a pile-up. · Soft send; the ball stays below the chest unless the sport needs a high set.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 2 · Tue Sept 8 – Fri Sept 11, 2026 Grades 1–3

September: Soccer, Terry Fox and football 4-day week: Mon Sept 7 off

1 Sharks and Dolphins

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

A tag warm-up with rescues, so nobody sits out.

Equipment: 2 noodles · marked sea · optional parachute

Set-up: Sea boundary. Two sharks. Show the freeze (T or agreed shape) and the rescue.

How we play:
  1. Sharks tag with noodles.
  2. Tagged dolphin freezes.
  3. A free dolphin rescues them (under the arms, high-five, or chute peek).
  4. Out of bounds = frozen.

Cues: Cross on the call — do not wait on the line. · Safe once both feet are over the end line or in a hoop. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Feet only in hoops — no diving. One or two per hoop for older grades. Tags are two-finger or noodle on the back or shoulder.

2 Traffic Lights (kick)

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Dribble, trap and stop on a colour: ball control at their own speed.

Equipment: Soccer balls, one per student if you can.

Set-up: Teach green / yellow / red with the sole trap. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Name the two jobs (attack / defend or the two end-lines) and which ball we are using.
  2. Green: dribble. Yellow: trap and wait. Red: stop, foot on the ball.
  3. Restart on green.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Green dribble, yellow trap, red sole-stop. · Eyes up. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

3 Through the Gates

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Partner passing and trapping, the first soccer skill of the unit.

Equipment: Cone pairs as gates, soccer balls.

Set-up: 6–10 gates. Partners. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Name the two jobs (attack / defend or the two end-lines) and which ball we are using.
  2. Send through a gate. Partner traps and sends back.
  3. Count fair gates, not speed.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Plant, inside foot, trap on the other side. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball. · Find a passing lane, not a pile-up.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 2 · Tue Sept 8 – Fri Sept 11, 2026 Grades 4–6

September: Soccer, Terry Fox and football 4-day week: Mon Sept 7 off

1 Ten-Second Tag

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Short bursts of chasing for a quick, fair warm-up.

Equipment: Centre line of cones, whistle.

Set-up: Split the gym. Taggers on one side, runners on the other. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. On the first whistle, a small group of taggers enters the runner half.
  2. Every 10 seconds, whistle again. Those taggers freeze. A new group goes in.
  3. A tagged runner does 5 jumping jacks on the spot, then keeps running.
  4. Rotate so every student is a tagger once.
  5. Play Ten-Second Tag in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Soft tag. · Jacks, then back in. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft tag. Taggers wait behind the line until the whistle.

2 Guard the Gates

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Dribble or pass past defenders who win the ball, not the body.

Equipment: Cone gates, soccer balls, pinnies.

Set-up: 4–6 gates. Two teams. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Attackers dribble or pass through a gate for a point.
  2. Defenders steal the ball with their feet only.
  3. Swap after 3 minutes.
  4. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.
  5. Play Guard the Gates in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Intercept, don’t contact. · Attackers dribble through, not around the wall. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

3 4-Goal Soccer

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Four nets keep a big class busy with lots of touches.

Equipment: Soccer balls, 4 goals

Set-up: Set 4 nets, one on each side of a square or gym. Four teams, each defending one net. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Teams may score in ANY net except their own.
  2. Use 2–3 soccer balls for a large group. Agree on goalie rules and whether a team can score in the same net twice in a row.
  3. Play timed quarters and optionally rotate which net each team defends.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball. · Find a passing lane, not a pile-up. · Soft send; the ball stays below the chest unless the sport needs a high set.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 3 · Mon Sept 14 – Fri Sept 18, 2026 Grades 1–3

September: Soccer, Terry Fox and football

1 Circle Racing

Locomotor & listen · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Steady running with a partner to get ready for the Terry Fox run.

Equipment: 1 cone per group of 4; 4 beanbags per group, each a different colour (for example red, blue, green, yellow); for 24 students, 6 cones and 24 beanbags

Set-up: Put one cone on the floor for each group. Space the cones at least 4 m apart and 2 m in from walls and the stage. Place 4 beanbags of different colours on the floor around each cone, about one big step out from the cone. Four players stand around each cone, just outside the beanbags.

How we play:
  1. Blow the whistle once. Players walk slowly around their cone in a clockwise direction.
  2. Blow the whistle again. Players switch and walk the other way.
  3. Keep switching directions with the whistle.
  4. Call two colours, for example "Green and yellow!"
  5. Players try to grab one of the two called beanbags. The two players who grab them win the round.
  6. Put the beanbags back, and play again. Play as many rounds as you like.

Cues: Walk, listen, react. · Eyes up while you walk. Know where each colour is. · Bend your knees and reach low. Do not dive.

Safety: Walking pace only. Groups at least 4 m apart and 2 m from walls. Grab low with hands; no diving or sliding on knees. Two players on one beanbag: let go and use Rock, Paper, Scissors. Stop signal: "Freeze."

2 Rob the Nest (dribble)

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Everyone dribbles at once to bring a ball home.

Equipment: 4 hoops, soccer balls.

Set-up: Four teams, four nests. Balls in the middle.

How we play:
  1. Dribble a ball into your nest.
  2. First to 3, or count on the whistle.
  3. Later round: you may take from another nest. No standing in the hoop.

Safety: No kicking people.

3 Avoid the Mines

Invasion & team · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Everyone dribbles at once with their head up.

Equipment: Many cones as ‘mines’; one ball per student

Set-up: Scatter cones across the gym.

How we play:
  1. Dribble through the space without touching a mine.
  2. Touch a mine = do a quick skill (3 toe taps) then continue.
  3. Add taggers or shrink the space.
  4. Switch to basketball or hockey dribble.

Cues: Dribble through the space without touching a mine. · Touch a mine = do a quick skill (3 toe taps) then continue. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: Soft balls, spread out, no slide tackles. Heads up when the ball is loose.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 3 · Mon Sept 14 – Fri Sept 18, 2026 Grades 4–6

September: Soccer, Terry Fox and football

1 Pair Running

Fitness & landings · Big-Group Games

Builds steady running for the Terry Fox run on Friday.

Equipment: None

Set-up: This is Paarlauf (“pair run”), a German relay method. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Partner A starts running a loop or shuttle. Partner B waits at the exchange point.
  2. A tags / hands off to B. B runs while A recovers. They keep exchanging so one partner is always running.
  3. Use a track, gym perimeter, or out-and-back cones. Set a time (3–6 minutes) rather than a distance so every pair stays moving.
  4. Coach even pacing and a gentle tag handoff — no shoving.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.
  6. After two rounds, 20 seconds of a named stretch, then one more quality set.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Quiet landings. Bend ankles, knees, and hips. · Quality beats speed. Stop if a wrist, knee, or back complains. · Breathe out on the work; do not hold a breath to rush.

Safety: Quiet landings. Stop a station if a wrist, knee, or back complains — switch to a walk option.

2 Collect Em All

Invasion & team · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Teams work together to win balls and carry them home.

Equipment: Hoops (one per team); foam balls in the centre

Set-up: Teams of 4–5 hold a shared hoop together at their corner.

How we play:
  1. Move as a team holding the hoop.
  2. Use feet only to kick one centre foam ball at a time back to your corner.
  3. Keep holding the hoop the whole time.
  4. Most balls at the end wins.

Cues: Move as a team holding the hoop. · Use feet only to kick one centre foam ball at a time back to your corner. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: Soft balls, spread out. Heads up when the ball is loose.

3 Pin Galore Soccer

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Every pin is a goal, so passing and shooting pay off fast.

Equipment: Plastic pins, indoor soccer balls or Softex foam balls

Set-up: Each team lines plastic pins along its end line. Two or more indoor soccer balls or Softex foam balls.

How we play:
  1. Play soccer with feet only.
  2. Score by knocking over an opponent’s pin instead of shooting into a net.
  3. Carry a knocked-down pin back and add it to your own row.
  4. The game ends when one team has every pin, or at time (most pins wins).

Safety: Foam balls. Kicks stay low — no blasting from close range. Nobody stands in front of their own pins as a goalie wall.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 4 · Mon Sept 21 – Fri Sept 25, 2026 Grades 1–3

September: Soccer, Terry Fox and football

1 Old Grey Cat

Tag & chase · Grades 1–4 · New Games

A simple chase game with one clear signal to run.

Equipment: None. Optional: 8–12 cones to mark two safe lines (the “trees”); 1 pinny or scarf for each cat.

Set-up: Use the centre circle (or mark one with cones). Mark a safe line (“the trees”) across each end of the gym with cones or use existing floor lines. Keep each safe line at least 3 m in from the end wall and the stage, so runners have room to slow down. Teach the chant before the first round.

How we play:
  1. The birds hold hands in a big circle. One player stands in the middle. That player is the old grey cat (give them a pinny or scarf).
  2. The birds walk around the cat in one direction and chant together: “We are weak little birds way up in a tree, you're an old grey cat and you can't catch me!”
  3. On the last word, the birds let go of hands and run to either safe line (the trees). The cat chases.
  4. Birds behind a safe line are safe. The cat tags with two fingers on the back or shoulder.
  5. The first bird tagged becomes the new cat. The old cat joins the circle as a bird.
  6. If nobody is tagged, the teacher picks a new cat.
  7. Everyone walks back to the circle, joins hands, and the next round starts.

Cues: Hold hands, walk the circle, chant together. · Let go, then go. · Eyes up, run to the trees. · Two fingers on the back or shoulder.

Safety: Safe lines coned at least 3 m from walls and stage. Birds let go of hands before running; no pulling or swinging the circle. Two-finger tag on the back or shoulder only. Eyes up, run forward, slow down after the line; no diving or sliding. Stop signal: teacher says “Freeze”. Students stop, hands on knees, eyes on the teacher.

2 Dash and Dribble

Relays & stations · Big-Group Games

A dribbling relay with a trap at the cone.

Equipment: Soccer balls, cones.

Set-up: Relay lines. A cone 8–12 m out. Even teams of 4–6. Lanes about 8–12 m, home cone behind a line. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. One runner at a time. Next player starts behind the home cone and goes on a high-five — not a shout from halfway.
  2. Dribble to the cone, trap, sprint back, tag.
  3. Next player goes.
  4. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.
  5. Play Dash and Dribble in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Trap at the cone before you turn. · Hand off — don’t roll at a teammate. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Wait behind the cone. Go on the high-five.

Safety: Eyes up at the turn. No long lines — more teams.

3 End Zone Ball

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Roll the ball to a teammate in the end zone: an easy first team game.

Equipment: 4–8 footballs or soccer balls, pinnies, optional mats as obstacles.

Set-up: Two halves. Each team names 2–3 end-zone catchers who stay in their end. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Players in their half roll balls to their own catchers.
  2. The other team tries to intercept rolls.
  3. A clean catch in the end zone scores.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Move after you pass. · Eyes up before you throw. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face. Walk on and off mats. No diving onto a house mat.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 4 · Mon Sept 21 – Fri Sept 25, 2026 Grades 4–6

September: Soccer, Terry Fox and football

1 Wolf’s Den

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Dodging past defenders, like a ball carrier finding space.

Equipment: Two end lines and a 3-m middle strip.

Set-up: Two wolves in the den. Everyone else on one end. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. On “Cross!” runners try to reach the far line without a tag.
  2. Tagged: 5 jumping jacks at the side, then help tag for one crossing only.
  3. Reset wolves every three crossings so the den does not fill forever.
  4. Rotate taggers every 45–90 seconds so the same three students are not chasing all period.
  5. A tagged player takes the next role or uses the game’s re-enter rule right away — nobody sits out.
  6. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Tag only in the den. · Jacks, then one turn as a helper. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft two-finger or noodle tags on the back or shoulder — never the head.

2 Crab Football

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

A low-key first football game that builds core strength.

Equipment: Playground ball, two end lines.

Set-up: Two teams. Short court. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Travel in a crab walk. Push or carry the sport ball to the line.
  2. 30–45 second rounds, then stretch.
  3. Swap if wrists are tired.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Hips up. Short bouts for wrists. · Uses the real sport ball. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

3 4 vs 1

Invasion & team · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Small-group keep-away for quick passes and getting open.

Equipment: Cones for a small grid; one ball per group of 5

Set-up: Grids about 8 × 8 m. Four attackers on the outside, one defender in the middle.

How we play:
  1. Attackers pass around the defender.
  2. Defender tries to intercept.
  3. After a touch or 45 seconds, rotate a new defender in.
  4. Count passes before an interception.

Cues: Attackers pass around the defender. · Defender tries to intercept. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: Soft balls, spread out, no slide tackles. Heads up when the ball is loose.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

1 Knock ’em Downers

Locomotor & listen · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Two jobs and nonstop movement: knock down or stand up.

Equipment: 20–30 cones or pins spread out; pinnies for two teams

Set-up: Scatter cones standing up across the gym. Split the class into Knockers and Pickers.

  1. On GO, Knockers tip cones over with a hand (or a foot in soccer month).

  4. Switch roles and play again.

2 Land and Sea

Locomotor & listen · Big-Group Games

Jump to land or sea on the call for body control and listening.

Equipment: A centre line.

Set-up: Name one side land, one side sea. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Spread out so you cannot touch a neighbour with an arm stretched. First command is a walk.
  2. Call land or sea. Students jump to that side.

  5. Play Land and Sea in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cross the gym past the octopus; tagged players become helpers.

Equipment: Two end lines.

Set-up: One octopus in the middle. Runners on one end. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. On go, runners cross.
  2. Tagged players stand with feet planted and become seaweed. They may tag with their arms.

  4. Rotate taggers every 45–90 seconds so the same three students are not chasing all period.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Seaweed plants both feet. · Arms tag — the body stays on the spot. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Feet stay planted for seaweed. No trips.

Relays & stations · Big-Group Games

Small touches through cones to sharpen close control.

  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

October: Football

1 Jellyfish

Tag & chase · Grades K–4 · New Games

A gentle tag game where tagged players become jellyfish helpers.

Equipment: 3 hoops to start, plus 3–6 spare hoops; court lines or boundary cones

Set-up: Use the basketball or volleyball court lines as the boundary. Keep it at least 2 m from walls and the stage. Choose 3 jellyfish. Each holds a hoop with both hands. Everyone else spreads out inside the area. They are the little fish.

How we play:
  1. On "Go," the jellyfish move around holding their hoops and try to tag the fish (two-finger tag on the back or shoulder).
  2. A tagged fish is "stung" and freezes.
  3. The jellyfish lifts the hoop over the frozen player's head, lowers it all the way to the floor, then lifts it back up over the head. That player is now "eaten."
  4. An eaten player moves to the perimeter (the edge of the boundary). Perimeter players can move anywhere along the edge, but not inside the area.
  5. Perimeter players try to tag any fish who comes too close to the edge. That fish also goes to the perimeter.
  6. When there are three players on the perimeter, call them over and give each a hoop. They enter as new jellyfish.
  7. Keep playing until only three fish are left. Those three are the jellyfish for the next round.

Cues: Two-finger tag on the back or shoulder. · Frozen means statue. The jellyfish does a slow halo, down and up. · Fish: use the open space in the middle, away from the edge.

Safety: Two-finger tag on the back or shoulder, below the head. Hoop moves slowly and never touches the head, face or neck. Jellyfish hold hoops with two hands, never swing them. Perimeter players stay on the edge line. Boundary 2 m from walls and stage. Stop signal: "Freeze."

2 Catch the Ice Cream

Target & send · Big-Group Games

Toss a beanbag into a partner’s cone: soft hands for catching.

Equipment: Cone and bean bag per pair

Set-up: Pairs stand a short distance apart, each with a cone.

How we play:
  1. Gentle toss to the cone.
  2. Receiver uses the cone only.
  3. Step back if consistent.
  4. Freeze on the whistle. Reset kit, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · One job at a time. Extra players fetch or count. · A miss is a short task, then back in.

Safety: No elimination. Soft two-finger or noodle tags on the back or shoulder — never the head. A miss is a short task, then stay in.

3 Captain Ball

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Pass to a captain in a hoop: a first passing game with a target.

Equipment: Soccer or playground ball, pinnies, 2 hoops.

Set-up: Each team has a captain in a hoop. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Pass toward your captain. Captain may catch but not run.
  2. Three completes, or a catch in the hoop, scores.
  3. Rotate the captain.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Captain stays in the hoop. · Three completes to score. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

October: Football

1 Predators and Prey Tag

Tag & chase · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Fast chasing and dodging to start football class.

Equipment: 1 pinnie or noodle for the bear; 2 hoops for the wolf pack; 2 mats as exercise stations (label one “Harder”, one “Easier”); cones for boundaries

Set-up: Cone a large rectangle at least 2 m in from the walls. Put the two exercise mats just outside one sideline.

How we play:
  1. Choose 1 Big Bear and 2 Wolves. Everyone else is a Pronghorn (a fast prairie animal).
  2. The two Wolves hold one hoop together, or each holds a hoop and they stay side by side as a pack.
  3. On “Go”, the bear and wolves try to tag Pronghorn with a two-finger tag on the back or shoulder.
  4. A tagged Pronghorn jogs to an exercise mat, chooses Harder or Easier, does the posted exercise (for example 10 jumping jacks or 5 squats), then rejoins the game.
  5. Twice per round the bear may call “Hungry Bear!” for a 5-second speed burst. Count the 5 seconds aloud with the class.
  6. At any time the teacher calls “Natural Disaster”: everyone freezes and does the challenge (stop, drop and roll; spin 3 times; balance on one foot for 5 seconds), then play resumes.
  7. Change the bear and wolves every 60–90 seconds.

Cues: Eyes up, find open space. · Two fingers, back or shoulder. · Wolves move as one. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher.

Safety: Boundaries 2 m from the walls and stage. Two-finger tags only, no pushing or grabbing clothes. Wolves keep the hoop low (waist height). Stop signal: one whistle means freeze, hands on knees, eyes on the teacher.

2 The Perfect Pass

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Teams complete passes before scoring, so everyone touches the ball.

Equipment: Soccer or playground ball, pinnies, two end lines or hoops.

Set-up: Two teams. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Carrier is frozen.
  2. Score only after 3 (or 5) completes.
  3. Intercepts reset the count.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Count the passes out loud. · Carrier is frozen. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

3 Football Frenzy

Invasion & team · Grades 3–6 · New Games

A busy whole-class game with foam footballs.

Equipment: 6 gym mats, 6 foam footballs, bean bags, 1 basket per team, a volleyball net (optional)

Set-up: Two teams start behind a line about 3 m from the centre, with bean bags in the middle. Put three mats on each end line, each holding one football. A basket sits at each team's end.

How we play:
  1. On “Go”, race to grab a bean bag and get back behind your line.
  2. Slide the bean bag along the floor (under the net if you use one) to touch an opponent's foot.
  3. If your bean bag touches a foot, you may run across, pick up a football from a mat and try a pass to a teammate.
  4. A catch goes in your team's basket. A miss returns the football to its mat.
  5. The first team to fill its basket wins the quarter. Reset and play again; everyone plays every quarter.

Cues: Slide low along the floor. · Step and throw, point to your target. · Show a target with your hands. · Freeze on the whistle — balls and bean bags down.

Safety: Soft foam footballs and soft bean-bag slides only; tag feet with the bean bag, not hands. Keep the space under the net clear. Stop signal: one whistle, balls and bean bags down.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

1 Fishbowl Tag

Tag & chase · Grades K–4 · New Games

An easy tag game with a safe fishbowl to rest in.

Equipment: 5 standing mats for the fishbowl, 1 rest-zone mat, 6 cones, 1 foam tag stick

Set-up: Stand the mats in the centre as a fishbowl with cones inside. Keep the fishbowl clear of the running path.

How we play:
  1. One tagger holds the foam tag stick. Everyone else moves around the space.
  2. A tagged player goes into the centre fishbowl.
  3. In the fishbowl, try to flip a cone upright within five attempts to rejoin.
  4. If the cone does not land upright in five tries, do five jumping jacks, then rejoin.
  5. Play is continuous. Change the tagger often.

Cues: Eyes up, find open space. · Soft tag below the shoulders. · Five tries, then back in. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher.

Safety: Soft foam tag stick only; tags below the shoulders. Keep the fishbowl clear of the running path. Stop signal: one whistle, freeze and face the teacher.

2 Hoop Rollers

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Roll a ball through a rolling hoop for aim and timing.

Equipment: 3–5 hoops per team (about 20–25 hoops for 6 teams); 1 foam ball (or soft dodgeball) per team; 1 cone per team at the far end; a start line (the baseline)

Set-up: Teams of 3–5 line up behind the baseline. Lay a line of hoops flat in front of each team at an appropriate distance (closer for younger students, farther for older). Place a cone at the far end of the gym opposite each team's line of hoops. Each team gets one ball to roll.

How we play:
  1. Relay style: one player at a time rolls the ball, trying to score it into one of the team's hoops.
  2. If the ball goes in a hoop, that player picks up the hoop and brings it back to the team.
  3. The player gets the ball, passes it to the next player and goes to the back of the line.
  4. Keep going until a team has captured all of its hoops.
  5. A team that has captured all its hoops moves to the cones at the far end. From there, it rolls into another team's hoops from the opposite side to try to steal them.
  6. A stolen hoop goes to the stealing team's pile. The game keeps going until time is up.

Cues: Opposite foot forward, bend low, roll smooth, follow through to the target. · Small hoop far away? Roll a little harder. Close hoop? Softer. · Choose a target hoop before you roll.

Safety: Soft balls only, rolled on the floor (no throwing). One roller per team at a time. Retrieve only when the lane is clear and walk on the side of the lane. Stealing teams roll from behind their far cones only. Hoops and cones 2 m from walls. Stop signal: "Freeze" (hold your ball).

3 Collect the Treasure

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Carry treasure home one piece at a time as a team.

Equipment: Beanbags, 4 hoops.

Set-up: Treasure in the middle. Team hoops in corners. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Carry one treasure home at a time.
  2. If tagged, walk it back to the middle.
  3. No standing in your hoop to guard.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: One treasure at a time. · Tagged = walk it back. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No body checks.

1 Zone Tag

Tag & chase · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Running through zones past a tagger, like finding a gap.

Equipment: 8–12 cones or floor markers to mark four zones; pinnies for the four taggers (optional); a whistle or music to start and stop

Set-up: Use cones or lines to cut the playing area into four zones (think four quarters of a gym floor or field). Pick four taggers and send one to stand in each zone. Everyone else scatters anywhere in the space.

How we play:
  1. On the signal, the runners move around freely and may run through any zone.
  2. Each tagger must stay inside their own zone. They can lean and reach, but they may not step across a cone line to chase.
  3. When a tagger gently tags a runner, they swap on the spot: the runner becomes the tagger for that zone, and the old tagger is now a runner and can go anywhere.
  4. Keep playing until the time is up. Freeze on the whistle.
  5. At the end, the four players who are taggers lead a short fitness challenge for the group (for example 10 push-ups, squats, or jumping jacks). Then pick four new taggers and go again.

Cues: Taggers: stay in your zone — you can reach, but not cross the line. · Runners: look up, cross the zones, change direction. · If you get tagged, swap places on the spot and take the next job. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher.

Safety: Soft two-finger tags on the back or shoulder only. Taggers stay in their zone, so runners must watch for others crossing lines at speed. Keep the zones large enough to spread out.

2 Capture the Flag Relay

Relays & stations · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Throw-and-catch practice at three distances.

Equipment: Per team: 1 cone for the team base, 3 hoops (near, middle and far), 15 flags or beanbags in a pile at the far end of the lane, 1 ball. Use foam or soft balls for grades 1–2 and foam footballs for grades 3–6.

Set-up: Make a lane for each team. At one end, put a cone as the team base and have the team line up behind it. Lay the three hoops in a line in front of the team at near, middle and far distances (for example about 3, 6 and 9 metres). Put the pile of flags or beanbags at the far end of the lane. One player stands in the near hoop as the catcher and the next in line is the first thrower.

How we play:
  1. The thrower stands behind the team cone and throws the ball to the catcher standing in the near hoop.
  2. If the catcher catches it, they run out to grab one flag or beanbag and carry it back to the team cone. That is a point for the team. The runner then joins the back of the line.
  3. At the same time the thrower steps in to be the new catcher. The next player in line becomes the new thrower.
  4. If the catch is missed, the thrower fetches the ball and throws again. The catcher stays in the hoop until a catch is made.
  5. After five flags are collected from the near hoop, the catcher moves back to the middle hoop. After five more, they move to the far hoop.
  6. Five more catches from the far hoop make 15 flags. The first team with 15 flags wins; everyone cheers for the other teams to finish.

Cues: Step, point, throw — to the catcher's chest. · Catch with soft hands and a stable stance in the hoop. · Run the flag back to the team cone. · Cheer on every team, not only your own.

Safety: Throw gently at a catchable height with two hands. Keep lanes wide apart and the flag pile out of the way. Runners stay in their own lane and walk the flag back if the lane is crowded.

3 Flasketball

Invasion & team · Grades 3–6 · New Games

Pass a foam football with no running, then shoot at the basket.

Equipment: 2–3 foam or junior footballs; basketball hoops; pinnies in 3–4 colours; floor markers or saucer cones to show scoring zones

Set-up: Mark three zones in front of each hoop: close (1 point), middle (2 points), far (3 points).

How we play:
  1. Split the class into 3 teams of 8 (or 4 teams of 6 and run two side-court games if the gym has side hoops).
  2. Two teams play; the third team practises passing at a wall station beside the court, then rotates in.
  3. Move the football only by throwing and catching. No running with the ball (like travelling in basketball). A player may pivot.
  4. Work the ball down the court and shoot by throwing the football at the hoop. A made shot scores the point value of the zone it was thrown from.
  5. After a basket, the other team takes the ball at the baseline and play continues.
  6. Play 3-minute games, then rotate teams.

Cues: Pass and move to open space. · Show a target with your hands. · Step and spiral, point to your target. · Freeze on the whistle — ball holder freezes too.

Safety: Defend with arms up, one arm's length away; no contact or stripping the ball. No shots while a defender is directly under the hoop. The waiting team stays behind the wall station line. Stop signal: whistle, ball holder freezes, everyone freezes.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

October: Football

1 Tic Tac Run

Tag & chase · Grades 1–6 · New Games

A relay with a quick thinking game at the end.

Equipment: 9 double-sided beanbags (mark X on one side and O on the other); skipping ropes or floor markers for a large tic-tac-toe board; cones or divider mats for a neutral zone; optional pinnies for the two teams

Set-up: Make a neutral zone at half court with cones or divider mats. Lay a large tic-tac-toe board on the floor at the end of the neutral zone, off to the side where runners will not cross it. Mark each team's safe zone (end line or a cone line) at least 2 m from the end walls. Divide the class into two teams: X team and O team. Each team starts on its own side of the neutral zone. Mark an X on one side and an O on the other side of all nine beanbags.

How we play:
  1. Say the rhyme, then flip a beanbag in the air: "Tic Tac Toe, three in a row, here we go. Don't be slow!"
  2. If the beanbag lands on X, the X team chases the O team back to the O team's safe zone and tries to tag them before they get there.
  3. If it lands on O, the O team chases the X team.
  4. Any player who is tagged switches to the other team for the next toss.
  5. If at least one tag is made, a player from the tagging team places a beanbag (showing their letter) on the tic-tac-toe board. Let a different student place the beanbag each toss.
  6. If no tag is made, no beanbag is placed.
  7. If the beanbag lands on its side, call a redo.
  8. Three in a row on the board earns one point for that team. Clear the board and reset to the original teams after each point.
  9. The first team to three points wins the day.

Cues: Ready position, eyes on the beanbag. · Chasers: two-finger tag on the back or shoulder. · Runners: turn and run straight to your safe zone. Run through the line, then slow down. · Placers: think. Block the other team or build your row.

Safety: Safe zones at least 2 m from end walls; runners slow down after the line. Two-finger tag on the back or shoulder, below the head; no pushing. Tic-tac-toe board off to the side, away from running paths. Divider mats (if used) stand firmly or lie flat. Stop signal: "Freeze."

2 Catch & Step

Strike & field · Big-Group Games

Partner throwing and catching that gets harder as you succeed.

Equipment: Type of ball, or water balloons

Set-up: Partners start close and play catch with a ball (or, outdoors in warm weather, a water balloon). Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. After every successful catch, both players take one step backward.
  2. On a drop, they take a step forward (or, if you are using beanbags, that pair is wet and rejoins with a ball).
  3. See which pair ends farthest apart after a time cap.
  4. Balls come back along the side. Restart on a teacher call, not a scramble through the middle.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out. · Hit, then run the path. Do not watch your own hit. · Fielders send to the base or hoop, not at a runner.

Safety: The ball is not thrown at a face. Balloons stay in the pair’s square. Tie extra balloons so they are not mouthed.

3 Steal the Bacon

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Listen for your number and race for the object.

Equipment: One object in the middle · two numbered lines

Set-up: Two teams on opposite lines, same numbers. Object centre.

How we play:
  1. Call a number (or two). Those players race the object.
  2. First hand on it tries to get back over their line. The other may tag.
  3. Soft tag only. Then reset.

Cues: Grab the object, not the person. · Soft tag the carrier. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face. Tags are two-finger or noodle on the back or shoulder.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 8 · Mon Oct 19 – Fri Oct 23, 2026 Grades 4–6

October: Football

1 Ambush

Tag & chase · Grades 2–6 · New Games

Dodge and change direction past hidden taggers.

Equipment: 1 hoop per attacker (start with 4–5 attackers for 24 students); boundary cones or court lines; pinnies for attackers (optional). Floor hockey version: 1 floor hockey stick and 1 soft ball or soft puck per attacker.

Set-up: Use the basketball court lines (or any marked area). Keep the boundary at least 2 m from walls and the stage. Choose 4–5 attackers. Each attacker starts with a hoop flat on the floor by their feet. Runners spread out inside the area.

How we play:
  1. On "Go," runners move around the area. Attackers kick their hoops along the floor.
  2. Attackers try to touch a runner's foot with their hoop.
  3. A runner whose foot is touched leaves the area, runs one lap around the outside of the boundary, then rejoins the game.
  4. Play for 2–3 minutes, then choose new attackers.

Cues: Hoop stays flat on the floor. Kick it with the inside of your foot. · Runners: heads up, light feet, use the open space. · Touched? Run your lap, then jump right back in. · Floor hockey: blade on the floor, push the puck, never lift the stick.

Safety: Hoops stay flat on the floor; no lifting, flipping or throwing hoops. Aim at feet only. Running shoes on. Lap runners stay outside the boundary and run in one direction only. Floor hockey version: stick blade below the knee at all times, push passes only (no slap shots), soft ball or puck only. Boundary 2 m from walls and stage. Stop signal: "Freeze" (put hoop or stick on the floor).

2 Punt to the line

Target & send · Big-Group Games

Practise the drop-kick, the last football skill of the unit.

Equipment: Football or playground ball, a line.

Set-up: 15–20 m to a line. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. One shooter at a time. Next waits behind the home cone. Fetchers stay to the side of the pin.
  2. Drop and kick before the bounce. Chase. Kick again until it crosses. Run it home.
  3. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.
  4. Play Punt to the line in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Drop, then kick. · Chase your own ball. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Opposite-foot step. Eyes on the target, not the teacher.

Safety: Throwing line is closed until fetchers are to the side. One object in the air per lane.

3 End Ball

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Pass only, and score with a clean catch in the end zone.

Equipment: Football or playground ball, pinnies, cones for two end zones.

Set-up: Each team names one catcher who stays in the far end. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Carrier cannot run and must pass in 5 seconds.
  2. A clean catch in the end zone scores. Rotate the catcher.
  3. Defend by intercepting, not by grabbing the holder.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Pivot, don’t run. · 5-second hold. Pass to space. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 9 · Mon Oct 26 – Fri Oct 30, 2026 Grades 1–3

October: Football

1 Tail Tag

Warm-up · Warm Up Games

Pull a tail, then hand it back so the game keeps going.

Equipment: Old clean socks, grocery bags, old cut-up ties, or touch football 'tails'

Set-up: Soft pulls on tails only. Tuck a tail in the back of pants (tuck long shirts). Spread out.

How we play:
  1. On GO, protect your tail and collect others. No grabbing bodies or clothes.
  2. Lost your tail? Keep playing — you can still steal tails.
  3. End: Timed round. Who still has a tail? Who collected 1, 2, 3…?

2 Target Toys

Target & send · Grades K–4 · New Games

Throw at fun targets for underhand and overhand aim.

Equipment: 8–12 hoops; a pile of small toys, stuffed animals or beanbags (3–5 per hoop); 1 foam ball per team, each team a different colour; a start line (court line or rope)

Set-up: Put the hoops flat on the floor at one end of the gym. Put several toys or beanbags in each hoop. Mark a start line an appropriate distance from the hoops (closer for younger students). Make 4–6 teams. Each team lines up behind the start line with its own colour of foam ball. Choose the skill: rolling or kicking. Students can also choose on their turn. Secretly choose three bonus items (for example "glasses, pig and robot"). Keep them in your head or write them on paper.

How we play:
  1. On "Go," the first player on each team rolls (or kicks) the ball toward the hoops.
  2. If the ball goes into a hoop, the player gets the ball and one toy from that hoop and brings both back to the team.
  3. If the ball misses, the player gets the ball and brings it back. Stay out of the way of other teams' balls.
  4. The player hands the ball to the next teammate and goes to the back of the line.
  5. Keep going until all the toys are collected.
  6. Count each team's toys. Then reveal the three secret items. Teams with a secret item get bonus points.

Cues: Step with the opposite foot, bend low, roll and follow through to the target. · Kicking: plant beside the ball, kick with the inside of the foot. · Get your ball, keep your eyes up, walk back on the side.

Safety: Foam balls only. Only one player per team in the target area at a time. Retrievers walk back along the side of the lane, never across other lanes. Waiting players stay behind the start line. Hoops 2 m from walls. Stop signal: "Freeze" (hold your ball).

3 Crab Football

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Push the ball with a crab walk: big fun and core strength.

Equipment: Playground ball, two end lines.

Set-up: Two teams. Short court. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Travel in a crab walk. Push or carry the sport ball to the line.
  2. 30–45 second rounds, then stretch.
  3. Swap if wrists are tired.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Hips up. Short bouts for wrists. · Uses the real sport ball. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 9 · Mon Oct 26 – Fri Oct 30, 2026 Grades 4–6

October: Football

1 Four Corner Tag

Tag & chase · Grades 3–6 · New Games

Read the taggers and pick the safest corner.

Equipment: 4 upright gym mats or 4 large cones as corners; 2 short foam noodle tag sticks (one per team); optional floor mats for waiting players; pinnies in 2 colours

Set-up: Stand the four mats in a large square in the middle of the gym, at least 3 m from the walls. Each team lines up at its own starting corner, on opposite corners.

How we play:
  1. Two teams. The first runner on each team holds that team's noodle.
  2. On “Go”, runners travel around the outside of the four corners, in the same direction, trying to catch and tag the other team's runner with the noodle.
  3. Runners make clean handoffs of the noodle to the next teammate at their team's corner, so fresh runners keep the chase going.
  4. One clean noodle tag on the back or shoulder earns one point. Restart from the starting corners after each point and rotate the lines forward.
  5. Rules: never run past a tag (if you are tagged, the point counts and you stop); no cutting inside the corners; no interfering with the other team's runner or handoff; no stalling at your corner.

Cues: Outside the mats every time. · Hand the noodle, don't throw it. · Next runner ready, hand out. · Freeze on the whistle — lower the noodle.

Safety: Short soft noodles only; tag below the shoulders, no swinging. Corners at least 3 m from the walls. Waiting lines stand back from the running path. Stop signal: one whistle, runners freeze and lower the noodle.

2 2-Ball

Target & send · Grades 3–6 · New Games

Two balls in play make players watch and pass quickly.

Equipment: Full basketball court with both hoops (the side hoops can be used too); cones to mark four corner jails; pinnies in 4 colours; 1 soft dodgeball as the throwing ball (one colour); 1 soft ball of a different colour as the kicking / jailbreak ball (slightly bigger if you have one). For big classes, add a second pair (one more throwing ball and one more kicking ball in the same two colours).

Set-up: Cone a jail in each of the four corners of the basketball court, at least 1.5 m in from the walls. Make four teams that are as even as you can, one per corner, in pinnies. Place the throwing ball and the kicking ball in the middle. Everyone starts inside their corner jail. Name the two balls out loud before Go.

How we play:
  1. On "Go" (or the whistle), everyone leaves the jails and play begins. House rule start: the first player to grab a ball from the centre carries it back to your team's corner before you throw or kick.
  2. The throwing ball is thrown to hit players, like dodgeball. After the start, you may not walk or run with it. If you do, you go to jail.
  3. The kicking ball is kicked to hit players. You may not pick it up or kick it up into your hands. If you do, you go to jail.
  4. If you are hit by either ball, you go into any jail you choose. A catch is a save. The thrower is out (to jail).
  5. No friendly fire: a hit on your own teammate doesn't count. Pass to teammates to move the ball around.
  6. If you step into a jail (for example while backing up without looking), you are in jail.
  7. Ways out of jail: tag a player who comes too close to your jail (you are free, and they go to jail); or, if the throwing ball rolls into your jail, throw it from the jail and hit a player in the game to be free.
  8. If the kicking ball goes into a jail, it becomes the jailbreak ball. Anyone in that jail may pick it up and shoot at the basketball hoop. A basket frees everyone in that jail. Only the kicking ball can be used for a jailbreak shot.
  9. Players in jail may move to any other jail at any time, for example to reach the jail where a ball has landed. They may not touch a ball that is in play while they move.
  10. Our no-elimination version: the video plays until one team is left. We don't. Play timed rounds of 4–5 minutes, then everyone resets to the corners.
  11. 30-second jail limit: if you are still in jail after about 30 seconds (a slow count, or one song chorus), do 5 jumping jacks and walk back in along the sideline. If more than half the class is in jail, call "Jailbreak all": everyone returns after 5 jacks.

Cues: Throw ball = hands. Kick ball = feet. Never switch. · Pass before you throw. Move after you send. · Eyes up when you back away from a jail. · Ball in your jail? Throw ball = hit to free yourself. Kick ball = shoot to free your whole jail.

Safety: Soft foam dodgeballs or soft playground balls only. Nothing hard for the kicking ball. Hits below the shoulders (below the waist for Grades 3–4, shoes and shins for 1–2). A ball at head height doesn't count, and the thrower goes to jail. The kicking ball stays low: no toe-blasting at close range, and no kicking a ball that is in someone's hands. Jail tags are a light two-finger tag on the shoulder or back only. Look where you are going: no backing up fast without looking, and no diving. Cone the jails at least 1.5 m in from the walls so players don't back into a wall. Jailbreak shots happen only from inside the jail; players in the game keep clear of the jail during a shot. Stop signal: the teacher says "Freeze". Stop, hold the ball still, hands on knees, eyes on the teacher.

3 Elementary Ultimate Frisbee

Invasion & team · Grades 3–6 · New Games

Pass and move into space, the same idea as football.

Equipment: Deck rings; pinnies; cone end zones

Set-up: Small-sided teams (4v4) with end zones.

How we play:
  1. Pass the deck ring; no running while holding it.
  2. Defenders keep one arm’s length.
  3. Score by catching in the end zone.
  4. Dropped or intercepted = turnover.

Cues: Pass the deck ring. · Defenders keep one arm’s length. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: Spread out. Heads up when the ring is loose.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 10 · Mon Nov 2 – Fri Nov 6, 2026 Grades 1–3

November: Floor hockey

1 Storm Chasers

Locomotor & listen · Grades K–6 · New Games

Simple calls and lots of moving to warm up for hockey.

Equipment: None. Optional: picture cards for each call (K–2).

Set-up: Push in the chairs. Each student finds a "storm spot" beside their desk or in an open space. Bubble check: arms out wide, spin slowly. If you touch anything, move over until you have your own space.

How we play:
  1. Teach the four calls: "Lightning": quick squat with hands on your head. "Puddle": two-foot jump on your spot. Land soft. "Wind left" or "Wind right": hop a quarter turn to face a new wall. "Rainbow": freeze in a big star shape.
  2. Say: "Show me ready position." Knees bent, weight on the balls of your feet.
  3. Start slow, then call faster and mix the calls up.
  4. If you make a mistake, do one clap (a "thunderclap") and jump right back in.
  5. Play for about 3 minutes. Take a breath break and a sip of water, then play again.

Cues: Ready position: knees bent, on the balls of your feet. · Land soft like a cat. · Listen first, then move.

Safety: Every jump and turn happens in your own spot. No spinning and no travelling across the room. Chairs pushed in, bags off the floor. Jump small, land soft, keep your bubble. Stop signal: "Freeze."

2 Hockey Dribbling Shapes

Relays & stations · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Everyone stick-handles at once, from simple to tricky.

Equipment: 1 floor-hockey stick and 1 soft ball per student (or 1 per pair taking turns), about 30 low cones, 4 tall cones.

Set-up: Set up three kinds of shapes around the gym, at least 3 m apart and 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors: cone lines (5–6 cones in a row), circles of cone gates (pairs of cones), and stars (one tall cone in the middle with 4 small cones around it). You can also use the gym floor lines as circles, triangles and squares. Practise “Sticks down!” before handing out sticks.

How we play:
  1. Step 1, simple dribble: dribble up the line of cones with small touches, stop the ball at the end cone, then dribble back.
  2. Add on: at the end cone, stop, step and push-shoot into a cone goal, then dribble back.
  3. Step 2, circle dribble: dribble through each gate around the circle, then turn and go the other way. You can also dribble along a gym line in a circle, triangle or square.
  4. Step 3, star dribble: start at an outside cone, dribble in around the middle cone, out to the next outside cone, back to the middle, and keep going until you are back at the start.
  5. Ball-handling extra: in your own space, small touches forward and back, then left and right.
  6. Everyone works at the same time. When sharing a shape, one student goes at a time.

Cues: Stay low, knees bent. · One hand on top of the stick, the other halfway down. · Small touches with the middle of the blade, both sides. · Head up to see where you are going.

Safety: Two hands on the stick, top hand on the end. The blade stays on or near the floor and below the knees at all times, including the follow-through: no slapshots and no lifting the ball. Push, don't slap. No body or stick contact. Use plastic-blade sticks with soft balls or light foam pucks, and check every blade before class. Keep boundaries, lanes and targets at least 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors. Carry sticks blade down when moving between stations. Stop signal: the teacher says “Sticks down!” Lay the stick flat on the floor, keep the ball still and eyes on the teacher. Shapes at least 3 m apart; one student per shape at a time when sharing.

3 Numbers Hockey

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Short, safe floor hockey games with sticks kept low.

Equipment: Floor-hockey sticks or hands, hockey ball, two cone goals.

Set-up: Two teams sit at the side, numbered. Pinnies on one team. Show the two attacking directions before GO. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Name the two jobs (attack / defend or the two end-lines) and which ball we are using.
  2. Call two or three numbers. Those players play to one goal.
  3. Sit and call a new set.
  4. Play 4–6 minute periods. Extra players are bumpers, walls, or the next wave — they stay in a job.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Your number only. · Sticks down on the whistle. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Head up. Pass or move — do not crowd the ball.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face. Sticks stay below the knee. No slapshots. Blade on the floor when you stop.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 10 · Mon Nov 2 – Fri Nov 6, 2026 Grades 4–6

November: Floor hockey

1 Secret Agent Tag

Tag & chase · Grades 2–6 · New Games

A new tag game where nobody knows who the taggers are.

Equipment: None. Court lines or boundary cones.

Set-up: Use the basketball court lines as the boundary. Keep it at least 2 m from walls and the stage. Everyone sits on the floor inside the area.

How we play:
  1. Say: "Eyes closed, heads down." Students close their eyes and put their heads down.
  2. Walk around and tap 2–3 players once on the head. They are the taggers (the source calls them "the bad guys").
  3. Tap 2–3 other players twice on the head. They are the secret agents (the freers).
  4. Everyone else is a citizen (a runner). Nobody tells anyone their role.
  5. Say: "Eyes open. You have 5 seconds to find a spot." Then blow the whistle to start.
  6. Taggers tag citizens and agents. A tagged player sits down where they are.
  7. A secret agent frees a sitting player with a tap on the shoulder. That player stands up and plays again.
  8. Secret agents can be tagged. A tagged agent sits like everyone else and can be freed by another agent.
  9. If all the secret agents are sitting at the same time, the round is over.
  10. Everyone sits, closes their eyes, and you choose new roles.

Cues: Two-finger tag on the back or shoulder. · Agents: free players quietly. Do not let the taggers see you. · Citizens: keep moving into open space. Watch who is freeing people.

Safety: Two-finger tag on the back or shoulder, below the head. No pushing or grabbing. Sitting players sit cross-legged with hands in their lap so runners do not trip. Runners look out for sitting players. Boundary 2 m from walls and stage. Role picking happens with eyes closed and sitting, so nobody moves until the whistle. Stop signal: "Freeze."

2 Gates & Hurdles Dribble

Invasion & team · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Dribble through gates and under hurdles for points.

Equipment: 1 stick and 1 soft ball per student, 20–30 cones (10–15 gates), 6–10 low hurdles (or pool noodles on cones).

Set-up: Scatter cone gates (pairs of cones about 1 m apart) and low hurdles around the gym, at least 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors. Each student starts in open space with a stick and a ball.

How we play:
  1. On “Go”, everyone dribbles at the same time with small touches.
  2. Tap the ball through a gate or under a hurdle, then move to a different one.
  3. Score 1 point for every gate or hurdle you get the ball through before time is up (45–60 seconds).
  4. You cannot use the same gate twice in a row.
  5. Play again and try to beat your own score.
  6. Gatekeepers (Grades 4–6): half the class stands in a gate with the blade on the floor. Dribblers tap through open gates. Gatekeepers block with the blade only, with no reaching into the dribbler. Swap roles every round.

Cues: Small touches, ball close. · Eyes up and find an open gate. · Slow down near others. · Blade on the floor.

Safety: Two hands on the stick, top hand on the end. The blade stays on or near the floor and below the knees at all times, including the follow-through: no slapshots and no lifting the ball. Push, don't slap. No body or stick contact. Use plastic-blade sticks with soft balls or light foam pucks, and check every blade before class. Keep boundaries, lanes and targets at least 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors. Carry sticks blade down when moving between stations. Stop signal: the teacher says “Sticks down!” Lay the stick flat on the floor, keep the ball still and eyes on the teacher. Eyes up and give each other space; one dribbler through a gate at a time; slow down near others.

3 Floorball

Strike & field · Big-Group Games

A small-sided game that uses the hockey ideas of attack and defence.

Equipment: Floor hockey sticks, soft ball, mini goals

Set-up: Goals at each end. One ball.

How we play:
  1. Tap the ball with the stick.
  2. After a goal, the conceding player restarts.
  3. Freeze on the whistle.

Safety: No elimination.

Next: School break (Nov 9–13). No school, no games that week.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

November: Floor hockey

1 Frozen Tag

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

A friendly freeze tag: a teammate frees you, so nobody sits out.

Equipment: Optional noodles · optional hoops for Hospital

Set-up: Show the freeze shape once. Show the rescue once. Soft tag only.

How we play:

Tiny touches with the blade on the floor through low cones.

How we play:

  2. Start on knees; progress to squat/hunker for harder saves.
  3. Play to 5, switch partners.

Cues: Slide the cone puck to score past your partner’s goal. · Start on knees. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Opposite-foot step. Eyes on the target, not the teacher.

Safety: Throw at targets, not people, and only from the line.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

Week 11 · Mon Nov 16 – Fri Nov 20, 2026 Grades 4–6

November: Floor hockey

1 Freedom Catch

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Tag where a throw and catch frees frozen players.

Equipment: Cones, foam balls

Set-up: Large coned field. Several taggers; free players have foam balls. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Taggers freeze runners in place with hands ready to catch.
  2. A teammate frees a frozen player by completing a catch to them.
  3. A drop leaves the player frozen (or freezes the thrower — pick one and teach it).
  4. Timed rounds; rotate taggers. Built for 50+ if space is big.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head. · Change pathway. Do not run someone over to make a tag. · If you are tagged, show it honestly and take the next job.

2 Zigzag & Shoot

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Dribble around cones, then shoot at a target.

Set-up: Each lane has a target beside the start (a folded mat on its side or a bench turned over), a small cone about 0.6 m out, a second about 1.2 m out and a third about 1.8 m out. Lanes at least 3 m apart and 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors.

How we play:
  1. Start with the ball next to the target.
  2. Zigzag around the first two cones, then circle the third cone.
  3. In line with the third cone, push-shoot back at the target.

Safety: Two hands on the stick, top hand on the end. The blade stays on or near the floor and below the knees at all times, including the follow-through: no slapshots and no lifting the ball. Push, don't slap. No body or stick contact. Use plastic-blade sticks with soft balls or light foam pucks, and check every blade before class. Keep boundaries, lanes and targets at least 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors. Carry sticks blade down when moving between stations. Stop signal: the teacher says “Sticks down!” Lay the stick flat on the floor, keep the ball still and eyes on the teacher. Lanes at least 3 m apart; shoot only at your own target; waiting players stand behind the start line.

3 Star Wars

Invasion & team · Big-Group Games

Teams aim at one big target ball, never at people.

Equipment: Beach ball, many soft balls, a bench at each end

Set-up: Beach ball on the centre line. Teams behind their lines.

How we play:

  2. Stay behind your line.
  3. Beach ball touches the other bench = 1.

Safety: No elimination.

November: Floor hockey

1 Shadow Tag

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Tag a shadow, not a body: safe chasing with sticks put away.

Equipment: Poly spots if you have no sun.

Set-up: Outdoor shadows, or indoor spots as pretend shadows. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Show the boundary, the freeze signal, and who starts as tagger before GO.
  2. Tag by stepping on a shadow or spot.
  3. Tagged player becomes the tagger, or does 5 jumps and re-enters.
  4. Rotate taggers every 45–90 seconds so the same three students are not chasing all period.
  5. Play Shadow Tag in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Soft feet on the shadow. · Switch taggers often. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft two-finger or noodle tags on the back or shoulder — never the head.

2 Fishing

Locomotor & listen · Big-Group Games

Hook cones with a noodle and bring them home: stick-style control.

Equipment: Pool noodle; scattered cones

Set-up: Scatter cones. Pair shares one noodle and a home hoop.

How we play:
  1. One hooks a cone, returns, passes the noodle.
  2. Continue until cones are gone.
  3. Freeze on the whistle.

Safety: No elimination.

3 Bottle Flip Hockey

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Shoot at bottles to flip and knock them: aim with the stick.

Equipment: Per lane: 1 stick, 1 soft ball, 2 small cones or spot markers for the goal, 1 spot marker, 1 plastic water bottle about one-third full with the lid on (or a cone).

Set-up: Each lane has a start line and a small goal 1.8–2.4 m away (two spot markers or small cones). Beside one goal post put a spot marker and the bottle (or a cone to flip). Lanes at least 3 m apart and 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors.

How we play:
  1. Push-shoot through the goal.
  2. After a goal, get the ball and dribble it back to the start line.
  3. Lay your stick flat on the floor beside the lane.
  4. Go to the goal post and flip the bottle until it lands upright on the spot.
  5. Pick up your stick with the right grip and shoot again.
  6. Count your goals in 1 minute, then rotate. Waiting players stick-handle in place behind the start line.

Cues: Push the shot along the floor. · Stick flat beside the lane before you flip. · Flip low. · Right grip before you shoot again.

Safety: Two hands on the stick, top hand on the end. The blade stays on or near the floor and below the knees at all times, including the follow-through: no slapshots and no lifting the ball. Push, don't slap. No body or stick contact. Use plastic-blade sticks with soft balls or light foam pucks, and check every blade before class. Keep boundaries, lanes and targets at least 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors. Carry sticks blade down when moving between stations. Stop signal: the teacher says “Sticks down!” Lay the stick flat on the floor, keep the ball still and eyes on the teacher. Lay the stick flat beside the lane, never on the walkway, before you flip. Flip low. Bottles with the lid on.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

2 Hockey pin knockdown

Target & send · Big-Group Games

One controlled shot after a dribble to knock a pin.

3 Move Up Hockey

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Each hit moves the target farther away: passing accuracy.

Equipment: Per lane: 1 stick, 1 soft ball, 4 spot markers, 1 empty plastic bottle or small cone (Cup Stack: 4 stackable cups or small cones).

Set-up: Each lane has a start line and four markers about 1.2 m, 1.8 m, 2.4 m and 3 m from the start. Put a light target (empty plastic bottle or small cone) on the first marker. Lanes at least 3 m apart and 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors.

How we play:
  1. Push-pass from the middle of the start line to knock over the target.
  2. Hit: move the target to the next marker, dribble the ball back to the start and shoot again.
  3. Miss: get the ball, dribble back and shoot again.
  4. After you knock over the target on the last marker, dribble back to the start to finish.
  5. Play a 1-minute challenge, or time how long it takes and try to beat your personal best. Partners swap: one shoots, one resets the target and counts.
  6. Cup Stack Hockey: put four stackable cups (or small cones) in a row 1.8–2.4 m from the start, about 30–45 cm apart. Any touch counts. When you hit one, stack it on another cup and dribble back. You finish when all the cups are in one stack.

Cues: Push-pass from the middle of the start line. · Look at the target, then the ball. · Follow through low, toward the target. · Dribble back, don't carry.

Safety: Two hands on the stick, top hand on the end. The blade stays on or near the floor and below the knees at all times, including the follow-through: no slapshots and no lifting the ball. Push, don't slap. No body or stick contact. Use plastic-blade sticks with soft balls or light foam pucks, and check every blade before class. Keep boundaries, lanes and targets at least 2 m from the walls, the stage and the doors. Carry sticks blade down when moving between stations. Stop signal: the teacher says “Sticks down!” Lay the stick flat on the floor, keep the ball still and eyes on the teacher. The partner resetting the target waits beside the lane, not behind the target, until the ball has stopped.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

November: Floor hockey

1 Turtle Tag

Tag & chase · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Flip onto your back like a turtle to be safe: silly and simple.

Equipment: Pool noodles for taggers
