How we play:
  1. Runners can drop onto their back like a turtle (arms and legs up) to be safe for up to 5 seconds.
  2. Longer only if a tagger is hovering.
  3. Tagged players do 3 jumping jacks, then back in.
  4. Switch taggers often.

Cues: Runners can drop onto their back like a turtle (arms and legs up) to be safe for up to 5… · Longer only if a tagger is hovering. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft two-finger or noodle tags below the shoulders. Nobody sits out.

2 Skittle Ball

Target & send · Big-Group Games

Underhand rolls at pins for aim, a lead-up to passing.

Equipment: Standing pins or cones · balls · a fetch line

Set-up: Pins out. Throwers on a mark. One fetcher at a time.

How we play:
  1. Underhand throw or roll at a pin.
  2. Knockdown = 1 point, or collect that pin and stack it at your base.
  3. Fetcher resets or delivers. Next thrower.
  4. Continue until pins are gone or time ends.

Cues: One throw, then fetch. · Safe at the pin line. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Opposite-foot step. Eyes on the target, not the teacher.

Safety: Throwing line is closed until fetchers are to the side. One object in the air per lane.

3 Bean Bag Battle

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

A team tossing battle to finish the hockey unit.

Equipment: Per battle (two teams): 1 laundry basket, milk crate or bin per team; 1 beanbag per team; 1 cone per team for the throwing line; 7 hoops in a row; 1 large cone (the marker) plus 1 cone at each end. For 24 students: 3 battles side by side, so 6 baskets, 6 beanbags, 21 hoops, 3 large marker cones.

Set-up: Make teams of 3–5. Pair the teams into battles. Each team lines up behind its cone. Place its basket an appropriate distance in front (closer for younger students). Lay 7 hoops in a row between the two teams of a battle. Put the large marker cone in the middle hoop and a cone just past each end hoop.

How we play:
  1. On "Go," the first player on each team tosses the beanbag at their basket. Use the toss you are working on (underhand or overhand).
  2. If only one team gets it in, that team moves the marker cone one hoop closer to the other team.
  3. If both teams get it in, or both miss, the marker does not move.
  4. The thrower gets the beanbag and hands it to the next player in line, then goes to the back.
  5. Keep going, one player at a time, relay style.
  6. When a team pushes the marker past the last hoop to the end cone, that team wins. Place the marker on top of the end cone.

Cues: Eyes on the target. Step with the opposite foot. · Underhand: swing low to high, follow through to the basket. · Overhand: side to target, elbow up, step and throw.

Safety: Beanbags only. One thrower per team at a time. Retrieve only after both throws land, and walk back along the side of the lane. Waiting players stay behind the cone. Battles at least 3 m apart. Hoops lie flat away from walking paths. Stop signal: "Freeze" (hold your beanbag).

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

1 Mystery Number Tag

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Secret taggers keep everyone alert and scanning.

Equipment: sticky notes, or pieces of paper

Set-up: Prepare sticky notes. A few say IT (or a special number); the rest are blank/free. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

  5. Play Battleships in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Stay in your zone. · Reset a pin; do not throw it back. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Opposite-foot step. Eyes on the target, not the teacher.

How we play:

  2. Defenders block.
  3. Reset and rotate defenders often.

Safety: No elimination.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 14 · Mon Dec 7 – Fri Dec 11, 2026 Grades 4–6

December: Games

1 Ten-Second Tag

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Short bursts of chasing for a quick, fair warm-up.

Equipment: Centre line of cones, whistle.

Set-up: Split the gym. Taggers on one side, runners on the other. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. On the first whistle, a small group of taggers enters the runner half.
  2. Every 10 seconds, whistle again. Those taggers freeze. A new group goes in.
  3. A tagged runner does 5 jumping jacks on the spot, then keeps running.
  4. Rotate so every student is a tagger once.
  5. Play Ten-Second Tag in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Soft tag. · Jacks, then back in. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft tag. Taggers wait behind the line until the whistle.

2 Hoop Hut Knock Down

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Build a hut together, then knock it down with a soft ball.

Equipment: 6 hoops per team; soft balls

Set-up: Teams build a 6-hoop hut: base, 4 upright, 1 on top.

How we play:
  1. Build the hut, run back to the line.
  2. Throw or roll soft balls to knock your own hut down for points.
  3. Rebuild and repeat.
  4. Most knockdowns in the time wins.

Cues: Build the hut, run back to the line. · Throw or roll soft balls to knock your own hut down for points. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Opposite-foot step. Eyes on the target, not the teacher.

Safety: Soft balls only. Throw at targets, not people, and only from the line.

3 Hidden Fleet

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Lob soft balls over the net to find the hidden ships.

Equipment: Volleyball net and standards; 1–2 parachutes or tarps draped over the net (or upright folding mats as a wall); 18 hoops (9 per team); 18 bowling pins or tall cones; 10–12 gator balls or soft foam balls

Set-up: Hang the parachute over the net so the two halves cannot see each other. Block the side gaps with mats.

How we play:
  1. Split the class into two teams of about 12, one on each side of the wall.
  2. Each team builds three ships with its 9 hoops: one of 4 hoops, one of 3 and one of 2, hoops touching in a line. Stand one pin in each hoop. Ships can go anywhere on that half.
  3. Each team gets 5–6 balls. On “Go”, players lob balls over the wall to try to knock down the other team's pins.
  4. A fallen pin stays down, even if your own team knocked it over.
  5. Get balls on your own side only and throw again.
  6. If a round drags, the teacher acts as “radar” and holds a pool noodle above one ship so the other side knows roughly where to aim.
  7. Play until one fleet is sunk, or for about two songs, then count the pins still standing. Rebuild ships in new spots and play again.

Cues: Step with the opposite foot. · High arc to clear the wall. · Call “ball” if one lands near you. · Freeze on the whistle — balls down.

Safety: Soft balls only. Lob over the wall, never under it at players. No reaching under or around the parachute. Keep 1 m clear of the net standards. Stop signal: one whistle, balls down, hands on heads.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

1 Wolf’s Den

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Runners cross the middle and tagged players help the wolves.

Set-up: Two wolves in the den. Everyone else on one end. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:

  2. Tagged: 5 jumping jacks at the side, then help tag for one crossing only.
  3. Reset wolves every three crossings so the den does not fill forever.

  5. A tagged player takes the next role or uses the game’s re-enter rule right away — nobody sits out.
  6. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Tag only in the den. · Jacks, then one turn as a helper. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft two-finger or noodle tags on the back or shoulder — never the head.

2 Cone Raider

Target & send · Big-Group Games

Partner throwing at cones: hit one and it becomes yours.

Equipment: 4-5 cones each; one tennis ball per pair

Set-up: Each partner sets a row of cones. Shared throwing line.

How we play:
  1. A throws at B's cones.
  2. Hit = take that cone.
  3. Miss = B's throw.
  4. Freeze on the whistle. Reset kit, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · One job at a time. Extra players fetch or count. · A miss is a short task, then back in.

Safety: No elimination. A miss is a short task, then stay in.

3 Fire the Cannons

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Throw to knock targets while teammates reload: aim and teamwork.

Equipment: Volleyball net lowered to about 1–1.2 m (or a rope between two standards); 4 throwing cones (one per team); targets on the far side: 8 hoops (1 point), 6 tall cones (2 points), 6 spot markers (5 points), 4 buckets or bins (10 points); per team, a set of soft throwables: 2 beanbags, 1 foam ball, 1 tennis ball, 1 foam football, 1 deck ring, 1 soft volleyball or trainer ball; tally sheet or whiteboard

Set-up: Set the net across the gym. Put 4 throwing cones in a row about 3–4 m from the net, at least 3 m apart. Each team lines up behind its cone. Scatter the targets 2–8 m beyond the net. Put the hoops closest, then tall cones, spot markers, and buckets farthest. Keep all targets at least 2 m from the far wall.

How we play:
  1. The first player in each line steps up to the throwing cone with the team's object for that round.
  2. Ready position: "Point to your target, scratch your ear with the ball, wait for my call."
  3. The teacher calls "Fire!" All four throwers send their object over the net at a target.
  4. Score: lands in a hoop = 1, knocks or hits a tall cone = 2, lands on a spot marker = 5, lands in a bucket = 10. The thrower calls their score; a teammate records it.
  5. The teacher calls "Collect." Only the four throwers go under or around the net, fetch their object, return, and hand it to the next player. They then go to the back of the line.
  6. The teacher calls "Fire!" again only when every collector is back behind the throwing line.
  7. Every round, the teacher names a new way to fire the cannon: Beanbag: underhand throw (swing back, point, step, follow through). Large foam ball: two-hand overhead throw. Tennis ball or foam football: overhand throw (opposite-foot step). Deck ring: backhand fling. Soft volleyball: underhand serve (fist, swing straight through). Foam football: drop punt. Indoor soccer ball: bounce and kick (Grades 3–6).

Cues: Point, scratch your ear, step, throw. · Step with the opposite foot. · Follow through to your target. · Fire on the call. Collect on the call.

Safety: Soft objects only, no hard balls. Throw only on "Fire!", one thrower per team at a time, and only at targets. Nobody passes the net until the teacher calls "Collect", and nobody throws until every collector is back. Throwing cones 3 m apart. Targets and the net standards padded or kept 2 m clear, and targets 2 m from the far wall. Stop signal: teacher says "Freeze". Students stop, drop objects, hands on knees, eyes on the teacher.

Next: School break (Dec 21–Jan 1). No school, no games that week.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

  3. Keep playing until the whistle.

Cues: Everyone tags. · RPS, then both stay in. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft two-finger or noodle tags on the back or shoulder — never the head.

2 Reaction Speed

Cooperative & circus · Big-Group Games

Catch the dropped ball: quick hands for passing.

Equipment: Trios: cone as a height marker, tennis ball

Set-up: Dropper holds the ball at chin height. Catcher ready.

How we play:
  1. Dropper releases with no fake.
  2. Catcher tries to catch before the bounce.

Safety: No elimination. Soft tags.

3 Jump Shot Handball

Invasion & team · Grades 4–6 · New Games

Jump, pass and shoot in a fast team game.

Equipment: 1 small soft ball per game (foam or gator-skin, about 15–18 cm); 4 portable goals, 2 side by side at each end (or 4 floor hockey nets, or cone goals 1.5 m wide); cones or floor markers to mark an arc about 6 m from each pair of goals (the basketball three-point line works); pinnies in 4 colours; 1 wall target (tape square) for the waiting teams

Set-up: Use the basketball court. Put two goals side by side on each end line, at least 2 m in from the end wall. Mark the arc (the defensive zone) in front of each pair of goals with cones or floor markers. The free-throw lane is the goalie area. With 24 students, make 4 teams of 6. Two teams play while the other two practise passing and jump-shot form at a wall target beside the court, behind a waiting line, then rotate. If the gym fits two courts across its width, run two games at once with one goal at each end of each court.

How we play:
  1. Each team puts 5 players on the court and 1 sub on the sideline. The sub swaps in after every goal.
  2. One player per team is the goalie and stays in the free-throw lane. Nobody else enters the goalie area except to get a loose ball.
  3. Move the ball only by passing and catching. No running with the ball. The player with the ball may pivot.
  4. You have a slow 3 seconds to pass or shoot. Count it aloud: "One-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three." If time runs out, put the ball down. The other team takes it.
  5. The ball must be passed once, player to player, before anyone can shoot. A pass from the goalie does not count.
  6. Only defenders may stand inside the arc. Attackers shoot from outside it. For a jump shot, take off from outside the line and release the ball in the air.
  7. Defenders guard the ball carrier from one arm's length, arms up to block passes and shots. No contact and no grabbing the ball.
  8. A goal scores 1 point. The goalie restarts play with a pass from the goalie area.
  9. Play 4-minute games, then rotate teams so the wall-station teams come on.

Cues: Pass and move to open space. · Show a target with your hands. · One-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three: pass or shoot. · Take off before the line, shoot in the air, land on two feet.

Safety: Goals and arcs at least 2 m from the walls and stage. Soft ball only. No contact: defenders stay one arm's length away. Shots stay below shoulder height. Only the goalie stands in the goalie area. Jumpers take off and land on the flat floor, not on mats or floor-marker edges. Waiting teams stay behind the wall-station line. Stop signal: teacher says "Freeze". Students stop, drop or hold the ball still, hands on knees, eyes on the teacher.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

  4. End: Keep removing until 3–4 hoops remain. Stand tall, at least one foot on a hoop, no pushing.

2 Jumping Jack Hoop Challenge

Fitness & landings · Big-Group Games

Spin a hoop, do jumping jacks, catch it, and add one.

Equipment: One hoop each; personal space

Set-up: Show a clean rim-spin and a two-hand catch.

How we play:
  1. Spin the hoop upright on the floor.
  2. Do 1 jumping jack, then catch.

3 Rope Hoop Scoop

Cooperative & circus · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Partners use skipping ropes to carry a hoop home.

Equipment: 24 skipping ropes (2 per pair); 24–36 hoops (mixed colours if you have them); 12 cones (one home cone per pair); optional colour-to-points chart (for example red 1, blue 2, yellow 3)

Set-up: Place 12 home cones around the outside of the gym, at least 2 m from the walls and about 3 m apart. Each pair starts at its cone with two skipping ropes. Scatter the hoops flat on the floor in the middle of the gym, spaced so pairs can reach them from different sides.

How we play:
  1. Each partner holds one end of each rope, so the two ropes run side by side between you, like a stretcher.
  2. On "Go", walk to any hoop on the floor.
  3. Slide your ropes under the hoop without using hands or feet on the hoop. Lift it together.
  4. Carry the hoop home to your cone and lower it next to the cone. That hoop is yours.
  5. If the hoop falls, stop where you are, slide the ropes under it again, and keep going. Nobody restarts from home.
  6. Go back for another hoop. The round ends when the last hoop on the floor has been collected.
  7. Count your hoops (or add up the colour points). Then play the "put back" round: carry your hoops back to the middle the same way.

Cues: Ropes low, slide under. · Ready, lift, together. · Walk when you carry. · Drop? Stop and scoop.

Safety: Home cones at least 2 m from walls and stage, about 3 m apart. Ropes stay low and are never swung or wrapped around hands, wrists or necks. Walk while carrying. Look up between hoops so pairs do not walk into each other's ropes. Stop signal: teacher says "Freeze". Students stop, drop ropes to the floor, hands on knees, eyes on the teacher.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

1 Ten-Second Tag

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Short bursts of chasing for a quick, fair warm-up.

Equipment: Centre line of cones, whistle.

Set-up: Split the gym. Taggers on one side, runners on the other. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. On the first whistle, a small group of taggers enters the runner half.
  2. Every 10 seconds, whistle again. Those taggers freeze. A new group goes in.
  3. A tagged runner does 5 jumping jacks on the spot, then keeps running.
  4. Rotate so every student is a tagger once.
  5. Play Ten-Second Tag in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Safety: Soft tag. Taggers wait behind the line until the whistle.

  2. Jump and land in balance.
  3. Stumble or hit = 5s rest.

Set-up: Scatter coloured hoops like a giant Twister board.

  2. Music off: call a body part and a colour (“right hand, blue”). Put that body part in a matching hoop.
  3. Sharing a hoop is allowed. Anyone who cannot get in does 5 reps and rejoins.
  4. Remove 1–2 hoops each round.

Safety: Spread out to arm's-length space. Look where you go. Step into hoops — no diving.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

  2. Herders tag ponies with a noodle touch on the hip or shoulder (not the head).
  3. A tagged pony must stand inside the nearest stable (hoop).
  4. Free ponies may rescue by joining hands and galloping a captured pony out of the stable without being tagged.
  5. Play 1–2 minute rounds and switch herders. Upbeat music optional.
  6. Rotate taggers every 45–90 seconds so the same three students are not chasing all period.

1 Card Pass Challenge

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Bump in a circle and beat the number on your card.

Equipment: Deck of cards; volleyballs

How we play:
  1. Draw a card — that’s the target number of passes.
  2. Bump/set in the circle trying to reach that many in a row.
  3. Beat the card, draw a new one.
  4. Face cards = 10.

Cues: Call “mine” before you touch it. · Flat platform, legs do the work. · Send it high to give your teammate time. · Freeze on the whistle — catch or hold the ball.

Safety: Keep groups at least 3 m apart. Do not chase a ball into another group; call “ball” and wait. Stop signal: whistle, catch or hold the ball, eyes on the teacher.

2 Hoop Collect (set/volley)

Relays & stations · Grades 1–6 · New Games

A relay to set or volley balls into your team hoop.

Equipment: Volleyballs or beach balls; one hoop per team

Set-up: Teams line up; balls at one end, team hoop at the other.

How we play:
  1. Pass the ball down the line using sets or volleys.
  2. The last player places it in the hoop.
  3. Collect as many as possible in the time.
  4. Rotate positions.

Cues: Pass the ball down the line using sets or volleys. · The last player places it in the hoop. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Wait behind the cone. Go on the high-five.

Safety: Lanes wide apart; stop at the cone, no diving for the finish.

3 NitroBall 2.0

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Volleyball meets four square with a waist-high net.

Equipment: Volleyball standards with the net lowered to waist height (or a rope between the standards); 1 four square / playground ball per court (beach balls or trainer balls for younger groups); floor markers or poly spots numbered 1–7 on each side; the free-throw lines as serve lines; pinnies in 3 colours; cones for a waiting line about 2 m from the court; 2–3 extra balls for the waiting team's wall passes

Set-up: Set the net across the middle of the court at waist height. For a class of 24, make three teams of 8: seven play and one waits to rotate in, and the third team waits to challenge the winner. Each side sets up seven players in a 3-1-3 (three in front, one in the middle, three in the back) on spots numbered 1 to 7, so students know exactly where to stand. Spot 4, the middle player, is the server. Cone a waiting line at least 2 m from the court, next to a side wall that is away from play, for the waiting team's wall passes.

How we play:
  1. Spot 4 serves underhand from behind the free-throw line. The serve has to land before the other team's free-throw line.
  2. The ball must bounce before every hit. Hit with an open hand or forearms.
  3. There is no out of bounds. The back wall and the ceiling are in play. If the ball bounces off and you can get to it, keep it alive.
  4. The ball must go over the net between the poles to count. Around the outside is no good.
  5. A server gets one mulligan (a redo) on their first serve after a rotation, and a deep serve counts. After you have served for a point, there is no mulligan.
  6. Teams rotate one spot when the receiving team wins the point, as in volleyball. The player waiting on the side rotates in.
  7. Off the backboard, onto bags or equipment, or into a corner: redo the serve, no argument.
  8. Games go to 11. The winners stay on and the waiting team rotates in. The team that comes off becomes the waiting team and starts its job right away: bump-set wall passes at the side wall, with one player keeping score for the court.

Cues: Let it bounce, then hit. · Spot numbers first, then play. · Between the poles counts. · Call "mine" and move your feet.

Safety: Before you play, check the ceiling and back wall (lights, basketball hoops, wall pads, stage edge). Move bags, carts and benches away from the walls, because the walls and ceiling are in play. Strike with an open hand or forearms only: no kicking, and no spiking down at players. No diving, sliding or running into walls to save a ball. Let it go. Call "mine" to avoid collisions in the 3-1-3. The waiting team stays behind a coned line at least 2 m from the court. Stop signal: teacher says "Freeze". Students stop, hold or drop the ball, hands on knees, eyes on the teacher.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

1 Sharks and Dolphins

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

A tag warm-up with rescues, so nobody sits out.

Equipment: 2 noodles · marked sea · optional parachute

Set-up: Sea boundary. Two sharks. Show the freeze (T or agreed shape) and the rescue.

How we play:
  1. Sharks tag with noodles.
  2. Tagged dolphin freezes.
  3. A free dolphin rescues them (under the arms, high-five, or chute peek).
  4. Out of bounds = frozen.

Cues: Cross on the call — do not wait on the line. · Safe once both feet are over the end line or in a hoop. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Feet only in hoops — no diving. One or two per hoop for older grades. Tags are two-finger or noodle on the back or shoulder.

2 Catch & Step

Strike & field · Big-Group Games

Partner throwing and catching that gets harder as you succeed.

Equipment: Type of ball, or water balloons

Set-up: Partners start close and play catch with a ball (or, outdoors in warm weather, a water balloon). Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. After every successful catch, both players take one step backward.
  2. On a drop, they take a step forward (or, if you are using beanbags, that pair is wet and rejoins with a ball).
  3. See which pair ends farthest apart after a time cap.
  4. Balls come back along the side. Restart on a teacher call, not a scramble through the middle.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out. · Hit, then run the path. Do not watch your own hit. · Fielders send to the base or hoop, not at a runner.

Safety: The ball is not thrown at a face. Balloons stay in the pair’s square. Tie extra balloons so they are not mouthed.

3 Bozo / bucket toss

Target & send · Grades K–3 · New Games

Underhand tosses into buckets at longer distances.

Equipment: Buckets at increasing distances; beanbags

Set-up: Rows of buckets set at close, middle, and far distances.

How we play:
  1. Underhand toss beanbags into buckets.
  2. Farther buckets score more points.
  3. Retrieve and rotate.
  4. Try non-dominant hand.

Cues: Underhand toss beanbags into buckets. · Farther buckets score more points. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Opposite-foot step. Eyes on the target, not the teacher.

Safety: Throw at targets, not people, and only from the line.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

  3. Change taggers each minute.
  4. Rotate taggers every 45–90 seconds so the same three students are not chasing all period.
  5. Play Survivor Tag in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: A tag is a skill, then you are back in. · Change taggers each minute. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft two-finger or noodle tags on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Three quick relays to finish the track unit.

How we play:
  1. Relay A — Scoop stack: Runner 1 carries one foam ball to the far cone, balances it as a scoop, and sprints back to tag the next player. First team to stack the set number of scoops without a collapse wins.
  2. Relay B — Build the cone: Cones start nested at home. Runners take turns carrying one cone out and stacking a taller ice-cream cone at the far end. Rebuild if it falls.
  3. Relay C — Take the order: Teacher calls an order (“3 scoops”). The runner must carry that many balls in one trip, place them on the cone, and return.
  4. Change locomotor skills between relays (run, skip, gallop). Use as a field-day rotation or a single lesson.
  5. High-five the next runner at home. First team sitting quietly after two rotations earns a cheer, then play a quality round.
  6. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Safety: Pass on the right. No diving at a hoop, pin, or beanbag.

June: Baseball

1 Mat Tag

Tag & chase · Grades 2–6 · New Games

Run the bases and stay safe on the mats.

Equipment: 4 mats (one per base); 2 soft foam balls or soft tags for the taggers (no hard dodgeballs — those stay on the Dodgeball page); pinnies for taggers

Set-up: Lay the four mats out like a baseball diamond, spaced far enough apart for a good run. Spread the class evenly across the bases, with any extras standing between bases. Choose one direction of travel (all runners go the same way). Pick two taggers, give each a soft ball, and send them into the space between bases.

How we play:
  1. On the signal, runners move from mat to mat in the chosen direction, one base after the next, round and round the diamond.
  2. A runner standing on a mat is safe. Set a limit of how many can stand on one mat at a time (for example six) so there is always room to move on.
  3. Runners leave a mat when the way is clear and run to the next one. They cannot go backward.
  4. Taggers try to touch a runner who is between mats, or gently toss or roll a soft ball at the runner's legs (below the waist).
  5. A runner who is tagged between mats becomes a tagger, and the tagger who made the tag becomes a runner. Hand the soft ball over, then everyone keeps playing.
  6. Stop at the whistle, change direction or taggers, and play another round.

Cues: Safe on the mat — then go when the path is clear. · Everyone runs the same way around the bases. · Look before you leave your mat. · If you are tagged, take the soft ball and become a tagger.

Safety: Throw soft balls underhand and below the waist, or tag with a gentle hand touch instead. Never throw at the head or face. Keep the mats flat and non-slip, spaced away from walls. Look before leaving a mat to avoid collisions.

2 Catch & Step

Strike & field · Big-Group Games

Partner throwing and catching that gets harder as you succeed.

Equipment: Type of ball, or water balloons

Set-up: Partners start close and play catch with a ball (or, outdoors in warm weather, a water balloon). Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. After every successful catch, both players take one step backward.
  2. On a drop, they take a step forward (or, if you are using beanbags, that pair is wet and rejoins with a ball).
  3. See which pair ends farthest apart after a time cap.
  4. Balls come back along the side. Restart on a teacher call, not a scramble through the middle.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out. · Hit, then run the path. Do not watch your own hit. · Fielders send to the base or hoop, not at a runner.

Safety: The ball is not thrown at a face. Balloons stay in the pair’s square. Tie extra balloons so they are not mouthed.

3 Continuous Kick Ball

Strike & field · Big-Group Games

Kickball where several runners can be on base at once.

Equipment: Playground or t-ball, saucer cone, bases or hoops.

Set-up: Two teams. Each kicker has a partner on the fielding team. Ball starts on a cone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Kick the ball off the cone and run. Several runners may be on base at once.
  2. Anyone may field, but only the kicker’s partner may place the ball back on the cone to stop play.
  3. Runners caught between bases when the ball is replaced are out of that run — they rotate, they do not sit the inning.
  4. A catch in the air is an out for that kicker only; other runners keep going until the cone is reset.
  5. Balls come back along the side. Restart on a teacher call, not a scramble through the middle.
  6. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Everyone kicks. · Throw to the base, not the runner. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

  3. Miss = pick up and try again.
  4. Freeze on the whistle. Reset kit, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · One job at a time. Extra players fetch or count. · A miss is a short task, then back in.

Safety: No elimination. A miss is a short task, then stay in.

3 Jailbreakers

Strike & field · Big-Group Games

A fair hit frees a teammate from jail.

Equipment: Tee or kick, t-ball, a jail hoop.

Set-up: Hitting team and fielding team. Jail hoop beside first. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Hit or kick and run.
  2. If the field stops the ball fairly, the runner walks to jail.
  3. The next fair hit frees one jailed runner.
  4. Everyone bats, then swap.
  5. Balls come back along the side. Restart on a teacher call, not a scramble through the middle.
  6. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Rescue is a tag and a walk home. · One rescue at a time. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out.

Safety: Throw to a hoop, not at the runner. Bat in a hoop.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

1 Everybody’s It

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Everyone can tag, so the whole class is moving from the first minute.

Target & send · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Throw tennis balls to knock volleyballs off cones.

Games of the Week · 2026–2027 · Mr. Fung

Week 39 · Mon June 21 – Fri June 25, 2027 Grades 1–3

June: Baseball

1 Back to Base

Locomotor & listen · Big-Group Games

Travel, then hurry back to your base on the whistle.

Equipment: Home hoops or spots.

Set-up: Assign bases. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Play any travel game.
  2. Whistle: everyone back to base.
  3. Last group leads a stretch, then plays again.
  4. If you miss a signal, skip the next one and rejoin — no extra laps as punishment.
  5. Play Back to Base in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Whistle means home. · Last group leads a stretch — they are not out. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Move the way I named (walk, skip, gallop) — not a race.

Safety: Give a hoop of space. Freeze means still feet — not a last-second shove.

2 Hoop underhand relay

Relays & stations · Big-Group Games

Three underhand tries to land a beanbag in the hoop.

Equipment: Beanbags, two hoops.

Set-up: Home hoop and a target hoop. Even teams of 4–6. Lanes about 8–12 m, home cone behind a line. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. One runner at a time. Next player starts behind the home cone and goes on a high-five — not a shout from halfway.
  2. Take a beanbag. Three underhand tries into the target. Leave a make. Home.
  3. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.
  4. Play Hoop underhand relay in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Step to the target. · Underhand. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Wait behind the cone. Go on the high-five.

Safety: Pass on the right. No diving at a hoop, pin, or beanbag.

3 Shark Ball

Strike & field · Big-Group Games

Kick and run for the far line past the shark.

Equipment: 1 foam ball

Set-up: Mark two safe end lines with a large open “ocean” in the middle. One foam ball only. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. Pick 2–4 sharks as fielders / taggers. Everyone else is a minnow / kicker.
  2. A minnow kicks the foam ball and immediately runs toward the far safe line.
  3. Sharks field the ball. With the ball they may tag a runner (ball-in-hand tag or a below-shoulder throw — decide first).
  4. A tagged runner becomes a shark. A runner who reaches the far line is safe and rejoins the kicking line.
  5. Keep the next kicker ready so the game never stops.
  6. Balls come back along the side. Restart on a teacher call, not a scramble through the middle.
  7. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out. · Hit, then run the path. Do not watch your own hit. · Fielders send to the base or hoop, not at a runner.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

June: Baseball

1 Blob Tag

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

The blob grows, so players must plan their escape routes.

Equipment: Optional noodles or cone hats · spare kit at the side

Set-up: Mark the court. Starters bibbed or holding noodles. Spare kit at the side if the blob needs gear.

How we play:
  1. Starters tag. Tagged player joins the blob (hold wrists, put on a cone hat, pick up a hoop).
  2. Only the agreed tag counts (noodle end, two fingers).
  3. When few runners remain, freeze, new starters.

Cues: Hold hands, do not yank. · Split at four. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

2 Strikeball

Strike & field · Big-Group Games

Strike the ball between players for placement.

Equipment: Ball

Set-up: Players stand in a circle, feet wide, one ball in play. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. The player with the ball strikes / rolls it, trying to send it between another player’s legs.
  2. That player tries to stop it with hands or by closing the gap (agree the legal save before you start).
  3. A ball that goes through scores a point for the striker, or the defender does a quick exercise — pick one.
  4. Keep the ball moving. Works in several circles for a large class.
  5. Balls come back along the side. Restart on a teacher call, not a scramble through the middle.
  6. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out. · Hit, then run the path. Do not watch your own hit. · Fielders send to the base or hoop, not at a runner.

Safety: The ball is not thrown at a face.

3 Diamond Strike

Strike & field · Big-Group Games

All four hitters run a base on any hit.

Equipment: 4 bases or buckets, t-ball, bats or hands.

Set-up: A square. One hitter at each base. Fielders around. A middle cone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. A fielder bowls underhand from the middle to any hitter.
  2. On a hit, all four hitters run one base clockwise.
  3. A catch in the air, or a ball placed on a base before a runner arrives, rotates that hitter to the waiting line.
  4. Everyone hits before teams swap.
  5. Balls come back along the side. Restart on a teacher call, not a scramble through the middle.
  6. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: One hit, everyone moves one base. · Field to the middle cone. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out.

Safety: Bowl from the middle only. No throw at runners.

House rules for every game: no elimination (a sit is a short task, then back in), freeze on the whistle, extra players get a job, and show a demo before the first play.

1 Octopus

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Cross the gym past the octopus; tagged players become helpers.

Equipment: Two end lines.

Set-up: One octopus in the middle. Runners on one end. Use the basketball lines as the boundary; cones mark any safe zone. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. On go, runners cross.
  2. Tagged players stand with feet planted and become seaweed. They may tag with their arms.
  3. When most are seaweed, pick new octopi. Seaweed stretch and re-enter as runners.
  4. Rotate taggers every 45–90 seconds so the same three students are not chasing all period.
  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Seaweed plants both feet. · Arms tag — the body stays on the spot. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Feet stay planted for seaweed. No trips.

Clap first, then catch: eyes on the ball.

Set-up: Show the three fail states: clap on a fake, drop, catch with no clap.

How we play:
  1. Throw or bounce to a player.
  2. They clap once, then catch.
  3. Miss = short task (5 marches) and they stay in. Next player.
  4. Relay version: clap-catch, then pass down the lane.

How we play:

  2. Fielders may not throw at the runner. They tag with the ball in two hands.

  5. Freeze on the whistle. Reset spots, then the next round.

Cues: Call before you catch. · Below-shoulder sends. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out.

Safety: No slide tackles, no body checks. The ball is not thrown at a face.

1 Ten-Second Tag

Tag & chase · Big-Group Games

Short bursts of chasing for a quick, fair warm-up.

Equipment: Centre line of cones, whistle.

Set-up: Split the gym. Taggers on one side, runners on the other. Agree the freeze signal before the first round.

How we play:
  1. On the first whistle, a small group of taggers enters the runner half.
  2. Every 10 seconds, whistle again. Those taggers freeze. A new group goes in.
  3. A tagged runner does 5 jumping jacks on the spot, then keeps running.
  4. Rotate so every student is a tagger once.
  5. Play Ten-Second Tag in short rounds so more students get the key job, then freeze and reset.

Cues: Soft tag. · Jacks, then back in. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Soft two-finger or noodle tag on the back or shoulder — never the head.

Safety: Soft tag. Taggers wait behind the line until the whistle.

2 4 Ball Kickball

Strike & field · Grades 1–6 · New Games

Four balls in play: fielders must decide fast.

Equipment: Four kickballs; bases

Set-up: Standard kickball diamond with four balls.

How we play:
  1. Four kickers kick at once.
  2. Fielders return all four balls to the pitcher’s zone to stop runners.
  3. Runners advance as far as they can.
  4. Adapt outs: stretch then back in.

Cues: Four kickers kick at once. · Fielders return all four balls to the pitcher’s zone to stop runners. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out.

Safety: Only the batter/kicker swings or kicks. Fielders stand well back and wait for GO.

3 Fun Kickball

Strike & field · Grades 2–8 · New Games

Six-base kickball to finish the year.

Equipment: Kickball; six bases

Set-up: Six-base diamond.

How we play:
  1. Kicker kicks and runs the six bases.
  2. More bases = more runners moving.
  3. Fielders throw to home to stop runners.
  4. Adapt outs — no sit-outs.

Cues: Kicker kicks and runs the six bases. · More bases = more runners moving. · Freeze on the whistle — then eyes on the teacher. · Ready position in the field — feet still, hands out.

Safety: Only the batter/kicker swings or kicks. Fielders stand well back and wait for GO.
